newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian border guards back at southern posts.
newsitem.headline: Albanian border guards back at southern posts.

text.p: Albanian border guards returned to posts along the Greek frontier on Monday and police patrolled the streets in nearby towns for the first time since rioting swept the region two weeks ago.
The guards, who fled in the face of a popular armed uprising across the Balkan country, went back to the posts which had been looted and sent out patrols along the border.
For almost two weeks the Albanian side of the border has been abandoned by security forces and controlled by gun-toting rebels after they ransacked customs buildings.

In other towns such as the village of Jergucati south of the rebel stronghold of Gjirokaster, 30 kms (20 miles) from the Greek border, police in full dress began to patrol the streets again and collect weapons from locals.
Thousands of Albanians throughout the southern region have been heavily armed since seizing army bases and making off with guns and ammunition.
In Gjirokaster, a main town and army base near the border, rebels began handing back tanks to police on Sunday and were trying to return all heavy weaponry.

Gjirokaster officials said they were having trouble finding places to store the returned weapons. Police also donned full dress for the first time in two weeks and were out on patrol as local officials tried to reorganise the town and restore order.
Rebels seized southern towns, looting arms depots, in a revolt against President Sali Berisha and in reaction to the collapse of popular investment schemes that wiped out savings.
Gjirokaster doctors, alarmed over conditions in hospitals, staged a protest on Monday and foreign aid workers arrived to assess the humanitarian needs of the region.
Doctors carried placards and banners to protest against the abundance of arms in the town, and called for guns to be banned from the hospital.
Many protesters held flowers and carried banners reading: "We don't want weapons in hospitals", "No to death" and "Long live Albania".
The doctors also appealed for medical supplies in southern Albania, where supplies were desperately short.
Doctor Islam Buti said hospital shelves were empty and appealed for medical aid from outside the country.
An International Red Cross team arrived in the region to visit hospitals and assess the needs.
"The Red Cross is touring Albania to evaluate the situation in preparation for sending supplies," Red Cross spokesman Amanda Williamson told Reuters Television.
Doctors have treated many people wounded by guns in recent weeks, mostly accidents during wild celebrations as the uprising swept one town after the next with almost no resistance.
